units.text: The June 2022 HTTP standard (RFC 9110) classifies POST as not safe; safe methods are GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE only.

citations.title: RFC 9110 Explained: Safe & Idempotent HTTP Methods

judgement.reason: The passages state RFC 9110 was published in June 2022 and that Section 9.2.1 defines four safe methods: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE, which excludes POST.

units.text: RFC 9110 (June 2022) explicitly lists POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, and PATCH as not safe in its safe-methods registry.

citations.title: What Is HTTP? HTTPS Difference, Methods, Status Codes and HTTP/3

judgement.reason: The passages state that POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, and PATCH are not safe and that RFC 9110 defines safe methods as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, but they do not explicitly show RFC 9110 listing these methods as not safe in a safe-methods registry.

units.text: Wikipedia HTTP article spans confirm POST is listed as not safe and safe methods exclude POST.

citations.title: What Is HTTP? HTTPS Difference, Methods, Status Codes and HTTP/3

judgement.reason: The cited Wikipedia passages explicitly state that POST is among methods that are not safe and list safe methods as GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, and QUERY, excluding POST.
